a_caldav_help: Reads free slots and writes appointments.
a_note: An app connected here is only offered to this assistant. Installing and credentials are handled once, in Apps.
a_payment_help: Sends a link instead of taking card details aloud.
a_smtp_help: Sends the confirmations this assistant writes.
b_cancel_help: Logged with who asked and when.
b_move_help: Only the caller’s own, after a match.
b_notice_help: Nothing closer than this is offered.
b_offered_help: Two is easier to answer on the phone than five.
b_server_help: Two-way. A slot booked here disappears from the calendar within seconds.
b_slot_help: Defaults per service come from the catalogue.
blurb_apps: The tools this assistant can reach while a caller is on the line.
blurb_booking: What the assistant is allowed to put in the calendar, and how far ahead.
blurb_contacts: How the assistant works out who is on the line before it says anything.
blurb_email: Before, during or after a call. The agent fills the placeholders from what was actually said.
blurb_forward: When the assistant stops answering and hands the call to a person.
blurb_instructions: Everything the agent should know that is not a document: how to open, what to refuse, who to hand over to.
blurb_knowledge: What this assistant is allowed to read. The library is shared — ticking a source here does not give it to the others.
blurb_persona: The first sentence a caller hears, and the voice that says it.
blurb_sms: Confirmations and reminders as text messages to the caller or a fixed number.
blurb_webhooks: Let your own software hear what happened, or answer the agent while the caller is still on the line.
c_ask_help: The caller is told their details will be kept.
c_create_help: Written after the call, from what was actually said.
c_dob_help: Asked only when two contacts share a name.
c_email_help: Used when the caller rings from a withheld number.
c_name_help: Compared against contact names before it asks again.
c_note: A match is never guessed out loud. If the assistant is unsure it asks rather than greeting the caller by the wrong name.
c_number_help: Exact match, then the same number without the country code.
c_ref_help: Read back digit by digit to confirm.
e_after_help: A summary of what was agreed, to the caller.
e_booking_help: The appointment, with the address and how to change it.
e_caller_help: Only when an email address is known or was given.
e_note: The agent fills the placeholders from what was actually said, and the sent copy is attached to the call so you can see what went out.
error_failed_title: This assistant could not be loaded
error_offline_title: The server could not be reached
f_asks_help: Rings that person’s extension for 20 s, then comes back.
f_distress_help: Straight to reception, no questions asked.
f_nobody_help: Takes a message and emails it.
f_note: The caller is told what is happening before the transfer, and hears music rather than silence while it rings. Ordered rules for the whole installation live in Routing rules.
group_act_note: Every one of these changes something outside Tel-Agent.
group_after_note: The caller cannot correct any of this, so keep it short and factual.
group_understand: It works out what they want
group_understand_note: The part that decides whether the call goes well.
hook_booked_desc: Sent when the assistant writes into the calendar.
hook_ended_desc: Sent after every call, with the transcript and what was agreed.
hook_stock_desc: The agent asks your software mid-call and waits for the answer.
i_note: Headings are only for you — the agent reads the whole thing. Short and specific beats long.
k_hours_note: Read as data, not as a document — so the assistant never offers a slot on a day you are closed. Shared by every assistant.
k_note: With nothing ticked the assistant still books and moves appointments, but every question about the business gets “I don’t know”.
not_found_body: It may have been deleted, or the link may belong to another workspace.
offline_body: Edit freely. The next call after registration returns uses whatever is saved.
offline_title: The line is offline — changes here are saved but nothing is answering
p_persona_note: A few sentences in your own words. The agent reads this before anything else.
s_message_help: A fixed template with placeholders. Never written by the model.
s_note: Per-message cost, unlike everything else here. Confirmations by email are free and reach the same people.
s_sender_help: Needs a number that can send SMS. Your current line receives only.
s_when_help: After the call, or the evening before an appointment.
save_failed: It could not be saved. Try again.
subtitle: {name} — {business} reception
t_answer_help: Above this the agent says “one moment” rather than leaving silence.
t_endpoint_help: How it decides the caller has finished. Semantic, not a silence timer.
t_maxlen_help: The call is wound up politely after this.
t_model_help: What decides the reply. A bigger model answers later; on a call that is worse, not better.
t_stt_help: Runs on every sentence the caller says.
t_voice_help: Runs on every sentence the agent says.
title: Edit assistant
w_note: An inbound webhook lets your own software answer the agent mid-call — a stock check or an appointment lookup. Anything slower than about two seconds and the caller hears silence, so keep the endpoint fast or the agent will apologise for waiting.
